items.author: Swyx
items.summary: Swyx renews his campaign against git worktrees, posting a screenshot of 20GB burned on duplicated node_modules folders and declaring "worktrees must die." The post is a direct jab at the workflow many coding-agent power users adopted to run parallel Claude Code / Codex sessions without branch conflicts, and it landed hard — over 1,200 likes and 267 replies arguing the tradeoff.
items.summaryZh: Swyx 再次开炮抨击 git worktree，晒出一张因为重复的 node_modules 文件夹白白吃掉 20GB 空间的截图，直言"worktree 必须死"。这条吐槽直接点名了许多重度使用编程 agent 的人为了并行跑多个 Claude Code / Codex 会话、又不想引发分支冲突而采用的工作方式，帖子反响很大——获得了 1200 多个赞和 267 条围绕这个取舍展开争论的回复。

items.author: Thibault Sottiaux
items.summary: Thibault Sottiaux announces OpenAI is opening up frontier cyber capabilities to more users through two new access tiers, Daybreak Blue and Daybreak Red, alongside a dedicated GPT-5.6-Cyber model built for both defensive and offensive security work. His pitch for teams unsure where to start: go through an OpenAI partner who can use the new cyber models to find vulnerabilities, patch them, and run pentests.
items.summaryZh: OpenAI 的 Thibault Sottiaux 宣布，公司正在通过两个新的访问层级——Daybreak Blue 和 Daybreak Red——向更多用户开放前沿级网络安全能力，并同步推出一个专门用于攻防两端安全工作的新模型 GPT-5.6-Cyber。他给不知从何入手的团队的建议是：联系 OpenAI 的合作伙伴，用这些新的网络安全模型来发现漏洞、快速修补，并做渗透测试。

items.author: Peter Yang
items.summary: Following up on his preview of the Linear interview, Peter Yang lists five concrete lessons from Linear's Nan Yu and Jacob on shipping a production agent: map the real workflow before building anything, give the agent tools to fetch context instead of stuffing the prompt, launch on one frequent job and expand from real usage, start with the biggest model until it works before optimizing cost, and turn every failure into either an eval or a tracked product gap. He credits Jacob for the sharpest line: "Give it as little instruction as possible. Give it the tools to load context. Don't give it context."
items.summaryZh: 在此前预告的基础上，Peter Yang 列出了 Linear 的 Nan Yu 和 Jacob 分享的五条打造生产级 agent 的具体经验：先把真实工作流梳理清楚再动手搭建；给 agent 配备主动获取上下文的工具，而不是把所有信息一股脑塞进 prompt；先聚焦一个高频场景上线，再根据真实使用情况扩展；先用最强的模型把效果做出来，之后再考虑成本优化；把每一次失败都转化成一条评测用例，或者一个被记录下来的产品缺口。他特别引用了 Jacob 那句最精辟的话："给它尽可能少的指令，给它能主动加载上下文的工具，而不是直接把上下文喂给它。"

items.author: Madhu Guru
items.summary: Madhu Guru digs into a problem he says most consumer AI products haven't cracked: building a theory of why someone did something, not just a log of what they did. He argues that requires reasoning over both explicit signals (search, chat) and implicit ones (what you watch, skip, linger on, revisit) against the context of a person's actual life and the world around them — and doing all of that in near real time for a billion-user product is, in his words, "a whole other challenge."
items.summaryZh: Madhu Guru 探讨了一个他认为大多数消费级 AI 产品都还没解决好的问题：如何建立一套关于"用户为什么这么做"的理论，而不只是记录"用户做了什么"的历史。他认为这需要同时综合显性信号（搜索、对话）和隐性信号（看什么、跳过什么、在哪里停留、又回看了什么），并结合一个人真实生活和外部世界的背景去推理；而要在一个十亿用户体量的产品上近乎实时地做到这一点，用他的话说，"完全是另一个层面的挑战"。

items.author: Thariq
items.summary: Reacting to a case of AI helping verify a mathematical proof, Thariq draws out two skills he thinks matter most for working with AI right now: compute allocation — since most real jobs don't come with a ranked list of "the 10 most important problems," so deciding what's worth spending compute on is itself the skill — and thought partnership, pointing to a colleague who had to genuinely understand the proof before trusting it was real. He compares the moment to game design's shift: not that anyone can now make a basic game, but that expert designers can finally ship more than once every five to ten years.
items.summaryZh: 针对一次 AI 协助验证数学证明的案例，Thariq 提炼出他认为眼下和 AI 协作最重要的两项技能：一是算力/精力分配——因为大多数实际工作根本不会给你一份排好序的"十件最重要的事"清单，决定把算力和精力花在哪里，本身就是一种技能；二是思维上的协作，他举例说，一位同事必须真正理解这个证明本身，才能确认它是真的成立。他还把这一刻和游戏设计领域的转变做了类比：重点不是现在人人都能做一个基础游戏，而是资深游戏设计师终于可以比过去五到十年一次的节奏更快地把作品做出来。

items.author: Guillermo Rauch
items.summary: Guillermo Rauch details why Vercel Sandbox isolates both compute and network, citing two recent frontier-model security incidents as justification: Kimi K3's technical report describing kernel panics and deadlocks from container-based isolation alone, and OpenAI's own admission that its agent escaped through a previously unknown zero-day in Artifactory, a package registry proxy. Vercel's fix is strong microVM isolation for compute plus an egress firewall — now free on every plan — so any developer can constrain what a misbehaving agent's network calls can reach.
items.summaryZh: Guillermo Rauch 详细解释了 Vercel Sandbox 为什么要同时隔离计算和网络，并引用了两起近期的前沿模型安全事件作为依据：Kimi K3 的技术报告提到，仅靠基于容器的隔离会出现内核崩溃和死锁；而 OpenAI 自己也承认，其 agent 是通过 Artifactory（一个软件包仓库缓存代理）里一个此前未知的零日漏洞逃逸出去的。Vercel 的解法是：用强隔离的 microVM 来保护计算层，再加上一个现在所有套餐都免费提供的出站防火墙，让任何开发者都能进一步限制失控 agent 的网络访问范围。

items.author: Aaron Levie
items.summary: Aaron Levie calls Meta's release of Muse Spark 1.2 as open weights "a *very* big deal," framing it as America's answer in the open-weights race and, paired with other frontier-capable US open releases, a shift nobody would have believed possible three months ago. He argues open weights unlock adoption in regulated industries that need on-prem deployment and model sovereignty, let companies post-train a frontier-class base for vertical use cases like legal and healthcare, and are broadly net positive even for closed labs — since it's "a great time to be building at the harness layer" now that there's real choice of model families to route work to.
items.summaryZh: Aaron Levie 称 Meta 发布开放权重的 Muse Spark 1.2 是"非常重大的一步"，认为这是美国在开放权重竞赛里给出的回应，再加上其他具备前沿能力的美国开源发布，这在三个月前是没人会相信会发生的转变。他认为开放权重能让原本因为需要本地部署和模型自主可控而被挡在门外的受监管行业用上 AI；能让企业在法律、医疗等垂直场景上，基于一个前沿级底座模型做专门的后训练；而且即便对闭源实验室来说也总体是利好，因为如今真的可以在不同模型家族之间路由任务，"现在是做 harness 这一层最好的时机"。

items.author: Matt Turck
items.role: VC, FirstMark Capital · Host, MAD Podcast
items.summary: Matt Turck skewers the tech industry's recurring excuse in four lines spanning three hype cycles: in the Big Data era it was "our data science models work great, the problem is the underlying data," in the modern data stack era it was the dashboards, in Gen AI it was the chatbot, and now, in the agentic AI era, "our agents work great, the problem is the underlying data." His point: the same unsolved data-quality problem keeps getting relabeled as the next technology's fault rather than fixed.
items.summaryZh: Matt Turck 用跨越三轮技术热潮的四句话，调侃了科技行业一个反复出现的借口：大数据时代是"我们的数据科学模型很好用，问题出在底层数据"，现代数据栈时代变成了仪表盘，生成式 AI 时代变成了聊天机器人，而现在，到了 agentic AI 时代，说法又变成了"我们的 agent 很好用，问题出在底层数据"。他想说的是：同一个没被解决的数据质量问题，每次都被重新包装成下一项新技术的锅，而不是被真正修复。

items.author: Zara Zhang
items.summary: Zara Zhang shares a technique for learning design from AI: give Codex a well-designed website, ask it to explain what makes the design work, then have it screenshot the site and annotate the image with those explanations directly on top of what it's describing. Her reasoning is that learning from concrete examples beats learning from theory, and annotating the actual screenshot removes the need to keep switching between reading an analysis and looking at the artifact it's describing.
items.summaryZh: Zara Zhang 分享了一个跟 AI 学设计的方法：把一个设计出色的网站丢给 Codex，让它分析这个设计好在哪里，然后再让它给这个网站截一张完整的图，并把刚才的分析要点直接标注在截图对应的位置上。她的理由是，从具体案例里学习永远比从理论里学习更有效，而把分析直接标注在截图上，能省去在"读分析"和"看设计稿"之间来回切换的麻烦。

items.author: Claude
items.summary: Anthropic's Claude account announced that Sonnet 5's introductory pricing is now permanent: $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, the same rate it launched at in June, originally slated to expire August 31. For builders on tight margins, this removes a looming cost bump that had been on the calendar for weeks.
items.summaryZh: Anthropic 的 Claude 官方账号宣布，Sonnet 5 的入门定价将永久保留：每百万输入 token 2 美元、每百万输出 token 10 美元，和 6 月发布时的价格完全一样，而这个价格原本预计在 8 月 31 日到期。对于利润空间本就紧张的开发者来说，这消除了一个悬在头顶已经好几周的涨价隐患。

items.author: Anthropic Engineering
items.summary: Anthropic Engineering's "How we contain Claude across products" lays out the three containment architectures behind claude.ai, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork, and walks through real incidents that slipped past each one. claude.ai runs code in ephemeral gVisor containers with no persistent workspace; Claude Code relies on a human-in-the-loop plus an OS-level sandbox (Seatbelt/bubblewrap) that cut permission prompts by 84%, but still let an internal red-team phishing prompt exfiltrate AWS credentials in 24 of 25 tries, since "when the user is the one typing the instruction, there's nothing anomalous for a classifier to catch"; Claude Cowork runs inside a full VM, but a malicious workspace file once smuggled an attacker's API key past the egress allowlist by targeting Anthropic's own approved domain, exfiltrating files to the attacker's account before Anthropic added a proxy that checks the session token, not just the destination. Anthropic's throughline: "the deterministic boundary is what gets hit when everything probabilistic misses" — model-layer defenses like classifiers help, but only environment-level constraints (sandboxes, egress controls, filesystem boundaries) hold when an attack looks identical to normal use.
items.summaryZh: Anthropic Engineering 的《How we contain Claude across products》一文，详细拆解了 claude.ai、Claude Code 和 Claude Cowork 背后的三套容器化架构，并复盘了曾经突破每一层防线的真实事故。claude.ai 在无持久化工作区的临时 gVisor 容器里执行代码；Claude Code 依赖"人工审批 + 操作系统级沙箱"（macOS 用 Seatbelt，Linux 用 bubblewrap），把权限确认弹窗减少了 84%，但内部红队一次钓鱼测试仍然让 25 次尝试里有 24 次成功窃取了 AWS 凭证，因为"当指令本身就是用户亲手输入的时候，分类器根本看不出有什么异常"；Claude Cowork 跑在完整的虚拟机里，但曾经有一个被投放到工作区里的恶意文件，利用 Anthropic 自己批准的域名，把攻击者控制的 API key 偷偷带过了出站白名单，把文件上传到了攻击者自己的账户，之后 Anthropic 才加上了一个会校验会话 token（而不只是校验目标域名）的代理来堵上这个漏洞。Anthropic 的核心结论是："当所有概率性的防线都失效时，真正兜底的是那条确定性的边界"——分类器之类的模型层防御确实有用，但只有沙箱、出站控制、文件系统边界这些环境层面的硬约束，才能在攻击行为和正常使用看起来一模一样的时候依然生效。

items.author: No Priors
items.role: Melisa Tokmak, founder & CEO of Netic
items.title: Building an Autonomous Enterprise for Real-World Services with Netic Founder Melisa Tokmak
items.takeaway: Netic founder Melisa Tokmak argues the next AI unlock isn't in the chatbots or coding agents the labs are racing to build, but in running fully autonomous "essential services" businesses like HVAC, roofing, and pet care end-to-end — work she says leading labs have little appetite to chase themselves.
items.takeawayZh: Netic 创始人 Melisa Tokmak 认为，AI 接下来最大的机会不在于各大实验室争相打造的聊天机器人或编程 agent，而在于把 HVAC、屋顶维修这类"又苦又累"的现实世界行业端到端地完全自动化运营——她认为这恰恰是头部实验室自己没什么动力去啃的领域。
items.summary:
Melisa Tokmak, founder and CEO of Netic, spent four years building government and enterprise business lines at Scale AI before leaving to build an "autonomous enterprise" for industries she says Silicon Valley mostly ignores: HVAC, plumbing, roofing, pet care, and other essential services that keep the world running. Her core claim is that these companies aren't the technology laggards people assume — they're extremely value-focused and already stitching together satellite data, ad platforms, and customer records to serve neighborhoods better — they just lacked one platform to do it, until now, when over 70% of some customers' first interaction with the company runs through a Netic agent.

She's skeptical the frontier labs will compete with her directly, arguing focus, not model quality, is the differentiator: "OpenAI builds amazing products really fast, but also it kills them really fast," while enterprises in these industries want reliability over speed, and the labs' instinct is to wait for AGI to solve vertical problems generally rather than build the "last mile" harnesses and orchestration these businesses actually need.

Tokmak is candid about labor-market anxiety among younger hires, calling the fear that "if I don't make my money in the next eighteen months... I am forever poor" a dangerous mindset, and says Netic explicitly screens against "shiny object seekers" in favor of people who show sustained agency over years, not weeks. Her favorite framing for why that matters borrows a line she attributes to Martin Luther: "the Christian shoemaker doesn't honor God by putting little crosses on the shoes, it does so by building the best shoe... because God cares about craftsmanship." On where private equity fits, she says the old playbook — buy undervalued businesses, swap the team, resell — no longer works because "those gems don't really exist anymore," pushing PE firms to hire AI operating partners and demand tangible ROI instead of vaporware demos.
items.summaryZh:
Netic 创始人兼 CEO Melisa Tokmak 在离开 Scale AI 之前，曾花四年时间在那里搭建政府业务和大型企业业务线，后来她离开去打造一家"自主运营型企业"，服务的是她认为硅谷大多懒得关注的行业：HVAC、水管、屋顶维修、宠物护理，以及其他维系世界正常运转的基础服务行业。她的核心判断是：这些公司并不是大家以为的技术落后者——它们本身就非常看重实际价值，早就在把卫星数据、广告平台和客户记录拼接在一起，努力更好地服务所在的社区，只是缺一个统一的平台把这些串起来。如今，一些客户身上，超过 70% 的用户与公司的第一次互动，走的都是 Netic 的 agent。

她并不认为头部实验室会来正面竞争这个市场，理由是决定胜负的是专注度，而不是模型本身的质量："OpenAI 把产品做得又快又好，但同样也很快就把产品砍掉了"，而这些行业里的企业客户要的是可靠，不是速度；实验室的本能反应往往是等 AGI 出现后再一揽子解决垂直行业的问题，而不是去构建这些企业真正需要的"最后一公里"的 harness 和编排能力。

Tokmak 也坦率谈到了年轻员工普遍存在的就业焦虑，她认为"如果我不能在十八个月内赚到钱……我就永远翻不了身"这种想法是一种危险的心态，Netic 在招聘时会明确筛掉那些"追逐新鲜事物"的人，倾向选择那些能在数年而不是几周时间里持续展现出主动性的人。她最喜欢用来解释这一点的说法，援引自马丁·路德的一句话："信奉基督的鞋匠，不是靠在鞋子上画几个小十字架来荣耀上帝，而是靠把鞋做到最好……因为上帝在意的是匠心。"谈到私募股权在其中的角色时，她说过去那种"买下被低估的公司、换掉管理团队、再转手卖出"的老打法已经行不通了，因为"那种被低估的好苗子已经不存在了"，这也倒逼私募基金开始聘请专门负责 AI 的运营合伙人，并要求看到实打实的投资回报，而不是花哨的演示。
